19 cells read as JSON. Prose only: markdown cells 0, 7, 12, 18 and the comments/printed strings in code cells 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, 15, 16. 20 edits.

The three known instances are confirmed and located: cell 6 source line 2 (file line 1289) "Email 024 is email 013 word for word"; cell 15 source line 6 (file line 1986) "013 and 024  the injected message and its clean twin"; cell 10 source lines 57-58 (file lines 1581-1582) "The fence is the only thing that changed." The notebook's own cell numbering is index+1 (cell ids run cell-01..cell-19), and every in-prose cross-reference in the file already uses that numbering correctly, so no reference numbers move.

Four more classes of the same defect were found beyond the three named. (1) The notebook never states that 013 and 024 are ground-truth malicious — cell 5 introduces 013 as "a benefits notice" and nothing corrects it, which is what lets "clean twin" read as true. Confirmed against builder/corpus/ground_truth.json: 013 malicious/credential_phish, 024 malicious/credential_phish, and 024's recipient is payroll@pellgrave.example while its body opens "Hello Tobias", exactly as the canonical note says. (2) The token cap is described twice as "the most one triage may spend" (cell 0 glossary, cell 14) — the framing the canonical wording exists to replace. (3) The escalation reasons are counted, not named, in cell 14 ("The five reasons"), and the list is now six. (4) Cell 18's written-answer prompt asserts "Your guardrails changed how your agent handled email 013" — the measurement points the other way (the fence does not stop the attack and no downstream control escalates it), and it asserts what a student's run will produce, so it is the highest-value edit in the file after the three named ones.

The fence repair has no prose anywhere in the notebook today; edit w6sol-07 introduces it in cell 8 where the markers are defined, and edit w6sol-06 adds it to the four-controls list in cell 7. Both carry the canonical sentence and the "no email in the teaching corpus carries a marker" caveat, so nothing reads as something a student watched happen.

Two things I did not spec, both PENDING. The schema check being wired as schema_problems (final-code-shape.md section 5) needs a prose statement of its limit — that indicators accepts any string, so a report history rides inside an allowed indicator and passes — but no canonical wording exists for it. And final-code-shape.md's grounding measurement (024 turns benign 0 of 8 without the known-good block, holds malicious 8 of 8 with it) is a number outside the canonical list, so edit w6sol-08 states the canonical sentence without the counts.

Note for the code pass: cell 9's SOLUTION comment now describes "the grounding" rather than "the facts", matching build_guarded_prompt() taking grounding_text(parsed). If the code lands with the parameter still named facts_text, edit w6sol-08 needs the noun changed back.

THE FIX (edit cap-row, high): line 119 said the cap limits "the tokens one email may spend" and that "passing it stops the run." It counts only the tokens the model wrote, summed across one triage, and no cap reads what the whole run costs. Replacement carries the canonical wording plus the reason a student sees it fire (a pre-written cell lowers it), and asserts nothing about what any student's run will produce.

WEEK 6 TERMS THAT CHECK OUT, no edit needed: prompt injection (126), confidence threshold (45), human review (88), fact check (69), facts block (70), data not instructions (50), hallucination (86), data exposure (48), data minimization (49), automation bias (30), overreliance (117), escalation (67). It is also the bolded definition on w6-content.md, and no canonical wording was settled for it, so I have marked it PENDING and low confidence rather than paste a wording of my own invention.
